notes: Check batch 2026-10-31, skill condition: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and a model_id matching their tier; every assistant message in each transcript carries the tier's model. Every result.json records head 551e3ab with uncommitted true and skill_hash 7945a7937b10ed3f7eb986faece5ef03f0883a6d5db35d2edcbd56504e5cadbf, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the dirty text graded here. Transcripts show Read calls on SKILL.md and references/ex_unit.md in all four and on references/processes.md in haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, not haiku-2, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md and processes.md) is met in 3 of 4. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changes since d04061d (git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/, committed plus the uncommitted Readability rewrite): of the eleven rules this case's index rows name, four changed or are new. "One expression per line, and tabular clauses" is new, with no earlier verdict. "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" is rewritten (nested calls and tuples are one expression, a multi-clause function need not be a table to keep `do:`, a one-line `if` has at most one computing branch, a `receive` on `do:` is a block, a `for` is always a block). "Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom" has a rewritten first bullet and an example. In ex_unit.md, "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" adds the sentence "A block named after a condition, or after a requirement where the project asks for that, still states a behaviour a failing test can contradict". The other seven (Run tests concurrently, Assert with patterns, Wait for messages, Start processes, Replace dependencies, Use setup, Open a module) are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-23 standard, with the 2026-10-29-check grading of the same shapes where 2026-10-23 had none.

"One expression per line, and tabular clauses" (new), constructs that exercised it, all clean. Deciding sentence for each: "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces." (1) Heads on `do:`: haiku-1 line 175 defp settle(server), do: :sys.get_state(server) and sonnet-1 line 10 def registry, do: @registry, a head and one expression each. (2) `->` clauses: haiku-1 line 156 and haiku-2 line 152, :stop -> :ok, a pattern and one expression, the only clause of its receive, so no table question arises. (3) Heads with several expressions: every test, setup, setup_all and helper (for example haiku-1 lines 161-165 defp exit_normally(pid) do with three steps, sonnet-2 lines 127-138 the exit setup) puts the sequence on the lines below the head, per "Those go on the lines below the head". (4) Nested constructs: the fn holding a receive (haiku-1 lines 153-159, haiku-2 lines 149-155) sits under its head inside a block; the one-line fns that bind nothing, sonnet-1 lines 176 and 186 start_supervised!({Agent, fn -> :ok end}) and sonnet-2 line 128 subscriber = spawn(fn -> Process.sleep(:infinity) end), are on body lines below a test or setup head, not on a head's line, and the capture rule's "A `fn -> now end` that binds nothing may stay on one line" is the construct-specific condition the new rule defers to ("the rules below apply it construct by construct"). No run has a multi-clause function, a multi-clause case or receive, or any other set of parallel clauses, so the table paragraph is not exercised. haiku-1 lines 137-139 (test "removes a subscriber killed from outside and keeps notifying the rest", %{ / server: server / } do) is a head mix format spread because the name is long; it holds one selection and its body is below, so it is not counted under this rule.

"Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (changed), constructs that exercised it, all clean. haiku-1 line 175 defp settle(server), do: :sys.get_state(server) and sonnet-1 line 10 def registry, do: @registry: decided by "A `do:` body is one expression on the head's line: a literal, a tuple, a field read, a comparison, or a call, nested or not." (the comment at haiku-1 lines 173-174 sits above the head, not in the body). The bodies holding a fn (haiku-1 lines 153-159 defp spawn_subscriber do, haiku-2 lines 149-155 the same) are blocks, per "or a `fn`, gets `do ... end`, however short it is". Both receives (haiku-1 lines 155-157, haiku-2 lines 151-153, receive do / :stop -> :ok / end) are blocks, so the sentence naming receive among the constructs that need do ... end is followed; the 2026-10-29-check violation shape, receive do: (:stop -> :ok), does not recur. sonnet-2 has no do: at all; every body is do ... end (clean, as 2026-10-29-check graded such files). No run has a one-line if/else, a for, a capture carrying a call with its own arguments (no capture at all), a multi-clause function, or a function that mixes the two forms, so the sum/2, if and for sentences have nothing to apply to.

"Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom" (changed): the deciding sentences would be "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short" and the kind-or-mode sentence, but no file contains a |> operator, so the rule is not exercised in 4 of 4, as in 2026-10-29-check.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" (changed in its describe half). The new sentence that decides the describe blocks is "A block named after a condition ... still states a behaviour a failing test can contradict", read with the case's own example ("when a subscriber exits", not "exits"). Condition blocks: haiku-1 113, haiku-2 106 and sonnet-2 126 "when a subscribed process exits"; sonnet-1 148 "when a subscribed process has exited" (with setup [:subscribe_and_exit]) and 173 "when an email subscriber and a process subscribe to one topic and the process exits". Each names the situation the rule's own ExUnit example names, not a bare topic: clean. Function-plus-condition blocks (haiku-1 "publish/3 to a pid", "publish/3 to an email address"; sonnet-1 "publish/3 to a process subscriber", "publish/3 to an email subscriber", "publish/3 to pid and email subscribers of one topic", "publish/3 on a topic without subscribers") name one function; sonnet-2 adds "start_link/1". No block joins two functions. Test names (unchanged half): haiku-1 13, all clean. haiku-2 14, all clean; 100 "returns :ok and keeps serving when the topic has no subscribers" names an effect beside :ok, clean as 2026-10-29-check haiku-2 "adds the subscriber to the topic and returns :ok". sonnet-1 16, all clean; 139 "sends nothing" and 167 "keeps the server running" borderline clean, as "does nothing for a topic without subscribers" in every earlier sweep; 156 "keeps the other subscribers of those topics" overstates its body (the test subscribes new subscribers after the exit rather than keeping earlier ones), which is an accuracy problem, not the forbidden shape, so not counted. sonnet-2 15, 3 violated: 44 "returns :ok for a pid" (body only line 45), 48 "returns :ok for an email address" (body only line 49), the same shape as 2026-10-29-check sonnet-1 lines 37 and 41, and 120 "succeeds for a topic without subscribers", which is the rule's own example of a name that only says the call did not fail ("succeeds with an empty cart"). Rule result: 1 of 4 violates (sonnet-2).

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`": sonnet-2 is the only run testing a start failure; line 39 assert {:error, {{%KeyError{key: :mailer}, _stacktrace}, _child}} = start_supervised(spec) calls start_supervised/1 and matches the reason, clean as every earlier sweep graded this match. No run calls start_link. Subscribers: sonnet-1 starts them with start_supervised!({Agent, fn -> :ok end}) and stops them with Agent.stop/1 (the test supervisor then restarts the permanent Agent under a new pid until the test ends; not a shape the rule names); the other three use bare spawn/1, clean as before.

"Wait for messages, not for time": every :DOWN pattern matches the caused reason: haiku-1 lines 164 :normal and 170 :killed; haiku-2 line 160 :normal; sonnet-1 line 197 :normal after Agent.stop/1; sonnet-2 line 135 :killed. Every refute_received follows a synchronous call (haiku-1 settle/1 = :sys.get_state/1 before refute_receive at lines 84 and 92; haiku-2 line 80; sonnet-1 lines 93 and 142; sonnet-2 line 114); sonnet-1 lines 103 and 122 use refute_receive with a 50 ms timeout, clean as before. No Process.sleep wait (sonnet-2 line 128 spawn(fn -> Process.sleep(:infinity) end) is a subscriber body, not counted, as before); sonnet-1 line 168 assert Process.alive?(server) is a one-shot assertion, not polling.

The other graded rules are clean in 4 of 4. All four use async: true with a setup_all Registry keyed by Module.concat(module, test) and a behaviour-implementing test mailer that finds the test pid through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); every server is start_supervised! under that name and setup returns a map matched in test heads; no Process.register, application env, :persistent_term, :meck or redefinition of Notify.Mailer. Every == has the call on the left; no elem/2, no bind-then-==; sonnet-1 lines 72-73 bind expected = [...] and compare the call to it whole, and sonnet-2 line 141 assert subscriber not in Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") is a membership check, both clean as before. sonnet-1 line 196 :ok = Agent.stop(pid) is a bare match inside the private helper stop_and_wait/1, not in a test body, so the sentence "In a test body, every match that can fail takes `assert` in front" does not reach it; not counted. Directive order: use then alias in all four.

Outside this case's list: haiku-1 lines 55-58 assert Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") == [ / "second@example.com", / "first@example.com" / ] is counted under "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call": mix format spreads the expected list over four lines (confirmed by formatting the one-line form in the scratch folder), and the rule says each argument is "a name, a short literal, or a trailing keyword list" and that "An assertion is a call like any other", with the fix binding expected first, which sonnet-1 lines 72-73 does; the rule's examples name a map, so counting a list is a judgment. sonnet-2 lines 69-70 assert Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") == / ["bo@example.com", self(), "ana@example.com"] is a formatter wrap after ==, with the list on one line, not counted. No capture, no -> clause over 70 characters, no comment that restates code (the comments at haiku-1 9 and 173-174, haiku-2 9 and 78-79, sonnet-1 12 and 92 give reasons).

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each: every run passed every time with no warnings or log output (haiku-1 13 tests, haiku-2 14, sonnet-1 16, sonnet-2 15). All four pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json.
